course.title: Atomic – Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics — Stage 9

unit.title: Fractions
unit.blurb: Recurring decimals as fractions, the order of operations with fractions, multiplying and dividing fractions and mixed numbers, and using number laws to make calculations easier.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Recognise fractions that give terminating or recurring decimals and convert recurring decimals to fractions.

O2.t: Use the order of operations with fractions, including powers and brackets.

O3.t: Multiply fractions and mixed numbers, simplifying and cancelling.

O4.t: Divide fractions and mixed numbers by multiplying by the reciprocal.

O5.t: Use the commutative, associative and distributive laws and simplifying to make calculations with fractions easier.

p: Write the fraction in its simplest form. If the denominator has **only the prime factors 2 and 5**, the decimal **terminates** (stops): 3/8 = 0.375, 7/20 = 0.35.
Any other prime factor gives a **recurring** decimal: 1/3 = 0.333…, 5/12 = 0.41666… A dot (or bar) shows the repeating digits: 0.4̇5̇ = 0.454545…
3/12 terminates, because it simplifies to 1/4. Always simplify before looking at the denominator.

p: **Commutative**: order does not matter for + and × (a × b = b × a). **Associative**: grouping does not matter for + and × ((a × b) × c = a × (b × c)). **Distributive**: a × (b + c) = a × b + a × c.
Subtraction and division are NOT commutative: 1/2 − 1/4 ≠ 1/4 − 1/2.
